angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 196,187 km at 211.78 pc = 0.01 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 4.7219 +/- 0.4783 mas (same row, RUWE 8.59): 211.78 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.282 +/- 0.074 solar radii from del Ser & Fors 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of EPIC 201170410.02 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.498.2778D/abstract): 196,187 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.287 +/- 0.101 solar masses from del Ser & Fors 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of EPIC 201170410.02 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.498.2778D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3648 +/- 172 K from del Ser & Fors 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of EPIC 201170410.02 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.498.2778D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: del Ser & Fors 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of EPIC 201170410.02 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.498.2778D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/epic-201170410.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.995, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
